clue.text: Confine one Frenchman to his bed

indicators.note: one and the Frenchman are put to bed, that is, tucked inside his bed

parts.note: the Frenchman's bed is a lit, the French word for bed
one is the Roman numeral I
M is short for Monsieur, a French man's title

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is ordered to stay in bed, perhaps by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed belongs to the Frenchman, so it is the French LIT; 'to' sends I and M into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit something is to restrict it within bounds, a close synonym of confine.

clue.text: Willingly dig when near the object sought

parts.note: to dig something is slang for to like it
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
in a hunting game you are hot when close to the hidden thing

explanation.surface: Someone digs eagerly as they near buried treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' looks like spadework but is slang for enjoy; 'hot' is the children's hunt call for getting close.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something like a shot means doing it at once and eagerly, without any hesitation.

clue.text: Equal in marriage

definitions.meaning: an equal is a peer or counterpart, someone of the same standing
a marriage is a union, as when a couple make a good pairing

explanation.surface: Partners in a marriage should be on an equal footing.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is both a peer who is one's equal and a wedding union, as in a love match.

clue.text: I suffer with internal disorder every few years

indicators.note: disorder tells us the letters are put out of their normal arrangement

explanation.surface: A patient complains of an internal complaint that recurs periodically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffer with' joins I to INTERNAL: I suffers along with it in the disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Triennial means occurring once in a cycle of three years, a regular interval of a few years.

clue.text: Worship a girl — one has to be in fashion

parts.note: Dora is a girl's name

indicators.note: one has to be in fashion, so the letter for one is placed inside the word for fashion

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or the fashionable set
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A suitor adores a stylish young woman and wants to be part of her fashionable world.
explanation.walkthrough: TON, meaning high fashion, is a crossword favourite from the French bon ton.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep reverence or love, the noun matching worship used as a noun.

clue.text: A written record included among some correspondence

indicators.note: the record is placed inside the word for some

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A diary entry is found among a bundle of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' poses as letters but means similarity.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogy is a likeness or parallel between two things, a correspondence in some respect.

clue.text: Exaggerated function got up to introduce composer

indicators.note: the reversed function takes the composer inside it
in a down entry, got up means read upwards, reversing the word

parts.note: a do is a party or social function
Giuseppe Verdi was an Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A grand function was arranged to present a composer, perhaps overdone.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'got up' means read from the bottom; the composer sits between the reversed letters, with 'to introduce' as the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to carry it too far, so overdid matches the past tense of exaggerated.

clue.text: The sacred river has a beginning

parts.note: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan

explanation.surface: A holy river has its source somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' joins the pieces; the river's 'beginning' is its source in the surface but the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha, the first Greek letter, means the start, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: I develop lumps — I have rash

indicators.note: develop suggests the letters grow into a new shape

parts.note: I have shortens to I've

explanation.surface: A patient reports lumps coming up and a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint beside the lumps but means hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulsive person acts on sudden urges without thought, rash in their actions.

clue.text: There's no holding a man who's good — or bad

indicators.note: the word for no holds the saint inside it

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: There's no stopping a good man, whether he's virtuous or wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' is a link; ST is the usual abbreviation for saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means unpleasant or wicked, a common synonym of bad.

clue.text: Bird in pool, say, disturbed water

indicators.note: say signals that the word for pool is only heard, not spelt the same

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money collected for shared use
a wake is the track of churned water behind a boat

explanation.surface: A bird floats on a pond whose surface has been churned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' looks like water beside the bird, but it is a pot of money, KITTY.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small gull of the North Atlantic, an example of a seabird.

clue.text: Churchwardens perhaps supply parts for church organs

definitions.meaning: a churchwarden is a long clay tobacco pipe
an organ produces sound through ranks of metal and wooden tubes

explanation.surface: The church officials are asked to provide components for the church's organ.
explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden here is not a parish officer but a long-stemmed clay pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name tubes: tobacco ones exemplified by the churchwarden, and the sounding tubes of an organ.

clue.text: Colourless female in the early stages of anaemia

indicators.note: the female is placed inside the opening letters
only the opening two letters of anaemia are kept and the rest dropped

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman looks pale as she begins to suffer from anaemia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The early stages of' keeps AN from anaemia; SHE goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a face drained of colour, grey and pale as ash.

clue.text: I'd obey all orders in court

indicators.note: orders here means arranges, telling us the letters are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A defendant promises to follow every instruction given in the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The OLD BAILEY is London's Central Criminal Court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Bailey is the popular name of England's Central Criminal Court in London, an example of a court.

clue.text: With great pleasure maybe receives a letter from overseas

indicators.note: the word for maybe takes in the Greek letter, holding it inside

parts.note: haply is an old word for perhaps or maybe
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, from abroad

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to get a letter from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic word for perhaps is the container, split after its third letter; a Greek letter is the one from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something happily means doing it gladly and willingly, with real delight.

clue.text: Head I had gift-wrapped

indicators.note: the gift wraps round the shortened I had, holding it inside

parts.note: a present is a gift
I had shortens to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone receives a nicely wrapped present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' poses as the start of a sentence but is the definition: a head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a republic, company or society, its chief.

clue.text: Isn't Ted smashing as a surgeon!

indicators.note: smashing means breaking up, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone admires Ted's brilliance as a surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' poses as British praise (great!) but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental surgeon is the formal title for one who treats teeth, so surgeon is a fair if loose description.

clue.text: Pen was, renovated for each journal

indicators.note: renovated means made over, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A writer's pen has been refurbished for each publication.
explanation.definitionFit: A journal can be a daily paper, so a newspaper is one kind of journal.

clue.text: Article reports country informally

parts.note: the is the definite article
states means reports or declares

explanation.surface: A newspaper article covers news from a country in a casual way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'informally' marks the definition as a casual name: THE STATES is everyday speech for the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans and others call the USA the States in casual speech, a colloquial name for the nation.

clue.text: Fencing right round American island

indicators.note: round turns the abbreviation for right the other way about

parts.note: Ellis Island in New York harbour was the immigration station for the United States

explanation.surface: A fence runs all the way around an island in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: ELLIS Island in New York harbour was the entry point for immigrants to the US; 'round' turns the abbreviation for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice of wooden or metal strips forming a light fence or screen.

clue.text: One in uniform points to cat

indicators.note: one goes inside the word for uniform

parts.note: uniform means the same throughout
one is the Roman numeral I
S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: A soldier in uniform gestures towards a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' poses as clothing but is the adjective meaning unvarying.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a breed of cat from Thailand, an example of a domestic cat.

clue.text: Confounding owner, he is right out of the running

indicators.note: confounding means throwing into confusion, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A racehorse owner is baffled to find his horse has no chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is the link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming nowhere in a race means failing to be placed, wholly out of contention.

clue.text: Gains this country eastern decoration, from Japan

parts.note: nets means gains, as in nets a profit
UK, the United Kingdom, is this country to a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Britain gains an oriental ornament imported from Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: A netsuke is a small carved toggle once worn on a Japanese kimono sash, an ornament.

clue.text: Fish with colourless lure

parts.note: white is colourless, without any hue
bait is something used to lure fish or prey

explanation.surface: An angler catches fish using a pale lure.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitebait are the tiny young of herring and sprat, eaten fried whole.

clue.text: Quiet game

definitions.meaning: an interjection calling for silence, like hush
a card game for four players in pairs

explanation.definitionFit: Whist is an old call for silence and also a trick-taking card game for two partnerships.

clue.text: Run over

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run not scored off the bat, such as a bye or wide
over can mean additional or left over, more than needed

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls, a sense that the clue uses only to mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a run given away in byes or wides is credited separately, and something surplus is additional.

clue.text: Assume I'll be in employment

indicators.note: be in tells us the I is placed inside the word for employment

parts.note: a post is a job or position of employment
I'll is I will: the I is kept and the 'll joins it to 'be in' as grammar

explanation.surface: Someone takes it for granted they will get the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'll of I'll is part of 'I will be in', a grammatical link.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as a basis for argument, to take as given.

clue.text: Is he afraid? Partly, as it's something of a shock

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man is frightened, since it comes as a bit of a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: A shock here is a stack of corn sheaves, not a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a group of sheaves of grain stood together in a field, so one bundle is part of it.

clue.text: Clumsy bird backed into it

indicators.note: into tells us the turned bird goes inside the word it
backed means the word for bird is set going backwards

parts.note: a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: An awkward bird reverses straight into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns PEN into NEP, which goes into IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill or competence, awkward and bungling.

clue.text: Crack soldiers wearing extraterrestrial gear

indicators.note: the soldiers are dressed in the alien, which surrounds them like clothing

parts.note: ET is the abbreviation for extraterrestrial, as in the film
a crack is a witty remark, a quip
men is a common word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Elite troops are kitted out in space-age equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like an adjective for elite soldiers but is a joke, QUIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment and gear both mean the tools and kit needed for a job.

clue.text: Four notes about a confidential meeting

indicators.note: the four notes go around the letter a, holding it in the middle

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, so four notes is te four times

explanation.surface: A short piece of music frames a private discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: The four TEs split two and two around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tete-a-tete, French for head to head, is a private conversation between two people.

clue.text: King William backed down before America

indicators.note: backed sends the word for down backwards

parts.note: down, soft hair or feathers, can mean fur
US is the abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: An English king retreats from his position ahead of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns the word for down; 'before' puts it ahead of America. William II of England was nicknamed for his red face.
explanation.definitionFit: William II of England was known by the nickname Rufus, Latin for red, from his ruddy complexion.
